_about: Translations of Cinematic Conversation Camera SF's settings page and listen prompt. Translate the values, never the keys; keep {} and other placeholders as they are. Anything left out or empty stays English. Save as UTF-8, and turn on your language's glyphs in SFSE Menu Framework's Fonts settings. Details: docs/TRANSLATING.md on GitHub.
Off: the whole mod stands down and conve: Off: the whole mod stands down and conversations use the game's own camera.
Standard, Close and Room are CCC's own. Frontier (a space western), Starborn (Kubrick and Interstellar), Constellation (a hard sci-fi documentary) and Nebula (a space opera) are CCC SF's.
How lively the cutting is, relative to t: How lively the cutting is, relative to the preset's own rhythm: -2 calmest, 0 the preset as designed, +2 liveliest. Each preset keeps its own: this changes the pace of the preset in use. Mostly felt in long speeches, as the camera cuts on each turn whatever the pace.
Push-ins, drifts, cranes and the like, a: Push-ins, drifts, cranes and the like, as each preset has them.
Keep the camera on one side of the line: Keep the camera on one side of the line between you. Off: each person is shot over their own side.
A close-up of the speaker on lines with: A close-up of the speaker on lines with an expression: always on strong ones, now and then on milder ones (how often is the preset's). The preset's own: none in Standard and Room, strong lines only in Close, every tier in CCC SF's presets.
A close-up of the NPC's answer to every: A close-up of the NPC's answer to every persuasion round, the verdict included, and to options with a skill check ([Intimidate], [Manipulate]...).
Cutting to you listening during their lo: Cutting to you listening during their longer stretches of talk, for one of their lines. The preset's own: off in CCC's presets, on in CCC SF's.
A close-up of you when you pick a [Persu: A close-up of you when you pick a [Persuade], [Intimidate] or similar option, for the line you say. The preset's own: on in CCC SF's presets, off in CCC's.
Your face answers the NPC's lines and yo: Your face answers the NPC's lines and your choices (the game keeps it neutral).
Wide: long shots keep a deep sharp zone. Cinematic: a shallow one everywhere.
0 a tripod, 100 fully handheld. The pres: 0 a tripod, 100 fully handheld. The preset's own: none in CCC's presets, Starborn 15, Nebula 40, Frontier 45, Constellation 50 with a slow handheld wander.
On: quest scenes you take part in (someo: On: quest scenes you take part in (someone walks up and starts talking, several people taking turns) keep the game's vanilla camera, which directs them. Everyday scenes (merchants, people chatting) keep this mod's camera. Off: this mod films every conversation.
Black bars across the top and bottom of: Black bars across the top and bottom of the screen while a conversation is filmed, like a film frame. They sit under the dialogue menu, so its subtitles and options stay on top.
Each bar's share of the screen's height. 0.12 is close to a 2.39:1 film frame on a 16:9 screen.
On: centred in the bottom bar while the: On: centred in the bottom bar while the bars are in. Off: where the game puts them (vanilla positioning, kept for mods that place subtitles themselves), which can overlap the top edge of the bottom bar.
The game hides your options during most: The game hides your options during most of their lines, but brings them back before some lines end. On: hidden for the whole of each line, back as it ends (except their greeting, where you pick an option while they speak). Off: as the game does.
Film people talking to each other near y: Film people talking to each other near you (the game's conversation scenes, not one-liners): a new shot for each line, letterboxed. Started with the listen prompt or on its own (below); moving ends it.
How near a conversation has to be, in me: How near a conversation has to be, in metres, to be offered or filmed.
A prompt to start filming with the liste: A prompt to start filming with the listen key (N, or hold B). Not shown while it starts on its own (the key still works then). With both off, nothing starts it.
As a conversation scene starts near you,: As a conversation scene starts near you, even while you walk or jog past (it holds you still until you let go of moving). No prompt then; the listen key still starts and stops it.
Start on its own while sprinting: Start on its own while sprinting
Also start as you sprint past a conversa: Also start as you sprint past a conversation (off: only while you walk or jog). With it on, a sprint past is stopped in its tracks.
A detailed log of what the camera does,: A detailed log of what the camera does, for bug reports: CinematicConversationCameraSF.log in Documents\My Games\Starfield\SFSE\Logs. Off normally (it costs a little).
A testing aid, off normally: each shot t: A testing aid, off normally: each shot the camera uses and why, and each line's expression, in the top bar.
Sets it back to its default ({}) and tak: Sets it back to its default ({}) and takes your change out of the _user.ini.
Back to the INI's value (removes your ch: Back to the INI's value (removes your change from the _user.ini).
Heads up: with \"Start on its own\" on,: Heads up: with "Start on its own" on, when a conversation scene starts near you, the camera is taken over to film it, and you're stopped where you are (looking around too) until you let go of the movement controls. Moving again ends the filming and gives you your controls back.
Changes apply from the next conversation: Changes apply from the next conversation (made during one, from the one after).
Changes go to CinematicConversationCamer: Changes go to CinematicConversationCameraSF_user.ini (with Mod Organizer, in its overwrite folder). More settings, each explained, are in CinematicConversationCameraSF.ini (Data\SFSE\Plugins).
The preset key (U) switches presets on t: The preset key (U) switches presets on the fly during a conversation.
